notes:
### New
- **Krate is now OpenCrate.** Same app, new name: your libraries,
  settings and backups stay as they are, and updates keep coming in as
  before. Downloads are at github.com/WhatMeansGithub/OpenCrate-releases.
- **Cue, loop and grid edits save themselves:** changes you make in the
  player go into your DJ library a moment later (backed up first; if the
  app is open, as soon as you close it), into the other libraries too if
  it's the primary library. Sync → Cue & grid edits is gone; the deck's
  EDITED tag now means "not in your DJ library yet".
- **Delete key:** in a playlist, **Delete** (or Backspace) removes the
  selected tracks after asking; **⌘-Delete** (Ctrl-Delete on Windows)
  removes them at once, as in Rekordbox. The same keys delete the
  selected playlist in the sidebar.
- **Tidy → Smart fixes → Repair broken dates:** finds files whose date tag
  apps can't read (e.g. a year written "25-08-2017", which Rekordbox shows
  as 25 and which hid the file's artwork) and puts the year (2017) into
  the file and your libraries. As with every fix, you see it first, the
  file is backed up and you can undo it.

### Fixes
- **Album art in Engine DJ:** tracks OpenCrate adds to Engine DJ (on your
  computer and on USB sticks) now get the cover from their audio file, so
  it shows in Engine DJ and on Denon players. Tracks OpenCrate added before
  without one get it with the next sync (the preview says how many).
- **USB sticks stay consistent with Rekordbox and Engine DJ.** Exports
  now mark the stick as your Rekordbox library's and keep each track's
  and playlist's number from the last export, so Rekordbox recognises its
  own tracks (it used to copy them again, and could crash), and the
  players' history keeps pointing at the right tracks.
- **No more duplicates in Engine DJ on the stick:** songs Engine DJ
  already has there (from its own export or its import of the Rekordbox
  export) are reused instead of added again, and aren't copied again.
  The preview now counts only the tracks that are really new.
- After exporting to a stick or ejecting it, the sidebar shows the
  stick's new contents straight away.
- **Sync in the player:** a synced deck takes its tempo from the track's
  typical beat, not the single beat under the playhead, so one odd beat
  (for example after moving beat 1) no longer sends it to a wrong tempo
  (a 132 BPM track jumped to 181 BPM) or makes the decks drift apart.
- **Downbeats are easier to see:** beat 1 of each bar is a solid red line
  with a marker at the top of the waveform.
